historical_references.context: The Treaty of Hudaybiyya was a peace agreement between the Muslims, led by Muhammad, and the Meccans. It was signed in 628 AD, allowing Muslims to perform Umrah (minor pilgrimage) the following year, with the condition that they would not enter Mecca that year. The agreement was named Sulh Hudaybiyy, meaning 'peace agreement of Hudaybiya'. After the Muslims returned in 629 AD to perform the pilgrimage, the Meccans broke their agreement, resulting in the Battle of Tabuk which ended with the Muslims returning to Medina without engaging the enemy.
